exact_notes_paragraphs.text: Source: pdlc_stage field and review decision record of each template, and the Commercialization Framework (the Concord). Concord mapping: Identify = Concept & Strategy (G0); Define = Design & Viability (G1 funds the build, G2 commits capacity on the solution design brief and delivery plan); Build = Build (G4 Commercial Readiness sign-off); Release = Beta and, where needed, Pilot; Go-to-Market = Launch (G5); Optimize = post-launch review (G6). G3 certification is conditional and runs in parallel when new payers or partners are involved. Implication: G2 commits capacity on the solution design brief and delivery plan, which is the content of the Technical Implementation Plan. The plan should therefore start before the capacity commitment, at the end of Define, even though the template places it in Build. Practices Map row: Prioritization sits inside the Opportunity Brief review decision, and Optimize corresponds to the Measurement and feedback row. Decision-makers follow the templates; the ownership matrix on the next slide still needs to be aligned for the Feature Brief, Technical Implementation Plan, and Testing plan approvers. AI row: agents documented in the Reconcile AI Agentic Spec-Driven Delivery document (the Release Agent is deferred until Product defines its outputs); none are documented yet for Identify, Define, Go-to-Market, or Optimize. The Technical Implementation Plan's section 6 requires named human review for any AI-assisted work.

exact_text_nodes: s widely between core platform and the Reconcile AI project
Sources: engineering and release working sessions, engineering survey (n=44), 2024–2026 release calendar. Working hypotheses to validate with Engineering.
No owned design step before build (readout finding 04); Core design knowledge sits with a small group. Recon: Architectural Specification template, Team Lead signs.
Core: Copilot in IntelliJ since January 2026, all gates human. Recon: epic-level agent pipeline. Other pods: developer-led, mostly unit tests.
Core regression is manual with one QA. Recon agents write Jest, Playwright, and Postman tests per story. XConnect ~100%; other pods partially automated.
Builds are tracked by ID, but release-night branch merges suggest production may be rebuilt rather than promoted: to confirm. Some new products not yet in CAB.
Survey: access delays, late test data, no read-only database access for troubleshooting. Recon waited months for production-like data.
DevOps, SRE, and incident roles are in place, but half of 2026 Core changes fell outside cadence; at least 5 of 11 patches were expired credentials or certificates.
Core plans in story points (~65 per sprint). Recon has proposed cycle time by stage, CFD, and control charts, not yet running. No DORA-style measures.
On both platforms, review, technical direction, and approvals rely on a few senior people; onboarding paths are thin. New onshore leads are being added.

exact_text_nodes: The single Build cell on the Practices Map hides two very different platforms. Working ratings to validate with Engineering.
Sources: engineering and release working sessions, engineering survey (n=44), 2024–2026 release calendar. Working hypotheses to validate with Engineering.
No owned design step before build (readout finding 04); Core design knowledge sits with a small group. Recon: Architectural Specification template, Team Lead signs.
Core: Copilot in IntelliJ since January 2026, all gates human. Recon: epic-level agent pipeline. Other pods: developer-led, mostly unit tests.
Core regression is manual with limited QA capacity. Recon agents write Jest, Playwright, and Postman tests per story. XConnect ~100%; other pods partially automated.
Builds are tracked by ID, but release-night branch merges suggest production may be rebuilt rather than promoted: to confirm. Some new products not yet in CAB.
Survey: access delays, late test data, no read-only database access for troubleshooting. Recon waited months for production-like data.
DevOps, SRE, and incident roles are in place, but half of 2026 Core changes fell outside cadence: defects, rollbacks, and credential or certificate fixes.
Core plans in story points (~65 per sprint). Recon has proposed cycle time by stage, CFD, and control charts, not yet running. No DORA-style measures.
On both platforms, review, technical direction, and approvals rely on a few senior people; onboarding paths are thin. New onshore leads are being added.

exact_notes_paragraphs.text: Engineering practices by platform. Ratings are working hypotheses built from working sessions with Reconcile AI engineering leadership, new-platform engineering leadership, Core engineering leadership, and release management, plus the engineering survey (n=44, March 2026) and the release calendar. 'To validate' means we have no evidence yet, not a low score. XConnect automation is ~100% in both the working session and the value chain deck; a ~70% figure is attributed to different products in different sources, so it is left off the slide. Release promotion: builds are tracked by ID through the in-house build system, confirmed by build numbers in the release calendar. Release management described merging the staging branch to production on release night, which suggests a rebuild; the Monday UAT / Thursday production cadence matches the Core releases in the calendar. Whether the staging-validated build is the one promoted to production is unconfirmed. The 'Addressed by' column links each practice to the recommendation that acts on it.

exact_notes_paragraphs.text: Release health baseline. Counts come from the consolidated release calendar: 2024–2025 from 'New builds' release emails, 2026 from the Deployments Team channel. The calendar lists Core applications (CHS, DCI, DCQ, CUSTCARE, REG, CRED, PNT, DWS, DEA and others); new-platform releases are not included. 2024–2025 emails did not label patches separately, so zeros for those years reflect recording, not absence. Credential and certificate patches: Salesforce client password expirations on 05/30 and 08/28 (the second followed by the 09/01 restoration of outbound Salesforce calls); BMA (04/07), DIL (05/11), and SSO (08/20) certificates applied as patches, where the calendar does not say whether they had expired. Defects that reached production: an ambiguous column name in DCI (03/23), a slow Custcare credentialing search (05/15), and a file-delivery failure for MET (07/15). Rollbacks: DEA (01/23) and DCQ (08/28). Two March patches (03/26 and 03/27) have no recorded cause.

exact_text_nodes: Recommendations summary: what should be done
Use this page as the leadership-level view before the detailed recommendation pages.
Set decision criteria, protect capacity, and make a 3-4 sprint view credible before commitments.
Clarify PM accountability for evidence, outcomes, adoption, and learning beyond the backlog.
Standardize the path from internal signal through PRD, epic, technical design, and plan.
Bring UX, Engineering, QA, Release, and Operations into feasibility work earlier.
Define the smallest release evidence path and feed post-launch results into the roadmap.
E1 Release stability and production quality
Review the root cause of unplanned changes; manage credentials and certificates as a lifecycle.
Automate the highest-risk regression first, reusing the patterns already working in Recon.
E3 Environments, access, and test data
Remove the waits for access and for realistic, masked test data.
Baseline and track release and flow measures on every platform, vendor team included.
Scale human-supervised AI practices with sanctioned tools, ahead of the December rollout.
Product recommendations are detailed first, then the engineering track. Both roll up in the two roadmaps at the end.
